newsitem.title: CHINA: China hails booming private economy in Tibet.
newsitem.headline: China hails booming private economy in Tibet.

text.p: China on Friday hailed the growing private sector in Tibet, saying employment by non-state enterprises in the remote Himalayan region had soared 1,000 percent since 1980.
Despite the growth in private enterprise in the region dubbed the roof of the world, official figures showed that the scale of most non-state ventures remained small.
The number of private businesses in Tibet had grown to 38,000 from 489 in 1980, with revenues totalling 59 million yuan ($7.1 million) in 1996, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Private firms employed 57,000 people last year, up 1,000 percent, while average capital rocketed to 10,000 yuan, the agency said.
The private sector accounted for 42 percent of total retail sales in Tibet, with private firms active in the transportation trade and hospitality industries as well, it said without giving details.
China has been eager to publicise economic success in Tibet, one of the nation's poorest regions and an area long troubled by sporadic pro-independence unrest.
Tibet's economy was forecast to grow by 10 percent to reach 7.35 billion yuan this year, surpassing the national growth rate for the first time, state media said in July.
